production.note: US model years. First: Edmunds 2022, "Higher-performing F1 Edition debuts", listing the "F1 2dr Coupe (4.0L 8cyl Turbo 8A)". Last: Edmunds 2023 lists the "F1 Edition Roadster 2dr Convertible (4.0L 8cyl Turbo 8A)" (edmunds-vantage-2023) and the C/D panel is a 2023 coupe (cd-vantage-f1-edition-2023); there was no 2024 US Vantage model year and the 2025 Vantage is a separate, 656 hp car (see the Vantage (2019–2023) record). Database sources for the years.

body.note: Panel: "front-engine, rear-wheel-drive, 2-passenger, 2-door coupe". Evo: "the new Vantage F1 Edition coupe and Roadster" (evo-vantage-f1-edition-reveal); the Roadster is treated as a separate car, as with the Vantage Roadster.

configuration.note: Panel: "twin-turbocharged and intercooled DOHC 32-valve V-8, aluminum block and heads, direct fuel injection".

fuel.note: Panel: "direct fuel injection" V-8; no hybrid system.

transmission.note: Panel: "TRANSMISSION 8-speed automatic". Evo: "specified exclusively with an eight-speed automatic transmission" (evo-vantage-f1-edition-reveal); no manual on the F1 Edition.

powerHp.note: Panel quote: "Power: 528 hp @ 6000 rpm". Evo: "features a 25bhp increase over standard to produce a total of 527bhp" (evo-vantage-f1-edition-reveal), a rounding of the same metric rating. Aston Martin rates its engines in PS; no Aston page with the F1 Edition's rating was opened, so powerStandard is 'Other' (C/D's US hp figure).

weightLb.note: Car and Driver road-test curb weight (weight-order step 2), 2023 F1 Edition Coupe, 8-speed automatic (the only transmission). Panel quote: "Curb Weight: 3813 lb". The test car had optional carbon-ceramic brakes ($11,100), which are lighter than the standard iron brakes, so a standard car may be slightly heavier. Aston Martin publishes only dry weights for this Vantage (the Vantage (2019–2023) record uses a 3,373 lb dry weight with lightweight options); a curb figure outranks that.
